summary: Deleted pmtiles-store.old-internal-disk (284GB), relieving disk pressure at the merge stage
check_pmtiles_integrity.py confirmed publish_cycle_12's local output has zero orphaned tiles (CLEAN)
publish_cycle_12 completed; deployed to stars production
Found stale duplicate child_z files at 50% of positions across pmtiles-store; deleted 212GB (leading hypothesis for the checkerboard artifact)
D74's deletion logic was flawed: it missed the downsampling layer's legitimate multi-child_z coexistence and over-deleted 4,396 files. Repaired with check_downsampling_done_integrity.py --fix
A coordinate-namespace collision between the aggregation and downsampling layers wrongly deleted 3,344 aggregation outputs. Repair via re-aggregation in progress

Reviewed the z7/z8 splice boundary: consistent with get_pmtiles_folder(), the boundary itself is sound. However, measurements confirmed up to 27.5% of z6-7 tiles remain missing over the seas around Japan even after the splice, due to Mapterhorn's own data limits

D74's diagnosis ("stale cleanup fails at 50% of positions") turned out to be wrong. Re-scanning with a correctly namespace-separated audit script found zero genuinely stale files. The checkerboard artifact's root cause is unidentified again

New leading hypothesis for the checkerboard artifact: aggregation_merge.py's per-512px-block blend decision may create discontinuities near coastlines (unverified). The cubicspline-instability hypothesis was ruled out by code inspection
Found a latent, never-triggered bug in downsampling_run.py --fix of the same kind as D76 (not run this session, no actual harm). Left in place pending Gen. 2's structural fix

The claim that "pmtiles cluster doesn't work" turned out to be an unverified, incorrect generalization from the extract limitation. To be tested in practice before the final merge, once japan-z8plus.pmtiles is rebuilt
